clearedSpotChecks.check: Rerun of battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py and replay.py for the seven chains (10, 8453, 130, 7777777, 480, 57073, 1868): every vector gave the specified word, every PoolManager script matched the Ethereum reference, and 16113 mined swaps gave 0 tick mismatches.
clearedSpotChecks.note: This is the item whose error would let a src/libraries computation differ on a chain, so it was checked first. The logs in op-stack-eth.work/out agree with the summary: battery.log shows 99985 of 99985 with 0 mismatches on all seven chains, targeted.log 85544 of 85544, pmdiff.log 250 of 250 identical, pmdiff2.log 300 of 300 identical, and the swaps.log per-chain counts sum to 16113 with 0 mismatches. I ran my own 22 edge vectors through eth_call with a code override on each RPC URL in networks.json on 2026-11-27. The vectors were MULMOD(max,max,max), MULMOD(max,max-1,max-2), ADDMOD(max,max,max-1), SDIV(-2^255,-1), SMOD(-2^255,-1), SMOD(-7,3), SIGNEXTEND at 30 and 0, SAR by 255 and by 256 of negative words, SHL by 256, SHR by 255, BYTE 31 and 32, EXP(3,255), EXP(0,0), DIV, MOD and MULMOD by zero, SLT, SGT and SUB underflow. All seven chains returned the specified word for every vector. The client versions reported were op-reth v0.0.0-dev-unknown (10), reth v2.5.2 base v1.5.6 (8453), op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 (130, 57073, 1868), conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 (7777777) and world-chain v2.8.2 (480), the same as clientver.txt. The 12 boundary cases on Optimism are explained by the code: Pool.sol:430-431 sets result.tick to step.tickNext - 1 after a zeroForOne crossing, so a price that sits exactly on a tick reports the tick below it. The deployed PoolManager runtime is 24009 bytes on six chains and 24050 on Unichain, and the hashes differ per chain because of immutables. The pmdiff runs used one bytecode under override, so they test the interpreter and not each deployed copy.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1290: op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 discard_tx 0x2d06750 clears the journal and all transient storage, so a failed transaction leaves no unlock flag, delta or count for the next one (PoolManager.sol:104-114).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I downloaded https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context/revm-context-43.0.3.crate this session (sha256 9b06efea511a15ff). In src/journal/inner.rs, discard_tx starts at line 174. It reverts every journal entry in reverse, then calls transient_storage.clear() at line 192, sets depth to 0 and increments the transaction id. commit_tx at line 141 also calls transient_storage.clear() at line 158 and clears the journal. The source therefore matches the research file. The binary mapping of 0x2d06750 to discard_tx was not repeated by me. I ran an on-chain test of the frame rules that Lock.sol and NonzeroDeltaCount.sol rely on within one transaction. A contract called itself twice through eth_call on all seven chains. The first subcall ran TSTORE(1,7) and reverted, and the second ran TSTORE(2,9) and stopped. The outer frame then read TLOAD(1)=0 and TLOAD(2)=9, with call results 0 and 1, on every chain. PoolManager.sol:104-114 sets the unlock flag in transient storage, runs the callback and reverts with CurrencyNotSettled if NonzeroDeltaCount.read() is not 0 at line 112, so a reverted inner frame cannot leave a delta behind. The research file's own lead on running commit_tx in the binaries stays open; on source reading the clear is present.

clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/protocol/hardforks/lagoon this session. It gives 1796918401 for the Sepolia chains and 1799683201 (11 Jan 2027) for OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink and Soneium, with status in development and mainnet activation subject to governance approval. The execution layer contents it lists are reduced BLS12-381 precompile input sizes, post-execution transactions and sequencer defined metering. src/ calls no BLS12-381 precompile. Post-execution transactions are inserted by the sequencer, and metering is set by the sequencer, so any hazard from them needs actor operator. cleared.json already records the sequencer defined metering refund path and the earlier Lagoon interop items. The superchain-registry op.toml I fetched has sha256 05fb9d7985da5106, which matches the prefix in the research file. I did not refetch the Base upgrades page or the other six registry files.
